title: Pocket regression clipboard — short-context hallucination spike
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for a regression I started chasing after the 2026-02 runtime push (kv-cache changes + batching tweak). Trying to capture examples, an ad-hoc rubric to triage impact, and next small experiments to run.

Context / What I saw:
- Deployed runtime change 2026-02-05: small refactor to KV cache invalidation logic (PR 1423) and a batching scheduler tweak to reduce latency for N<8.
- Starting 2026-02-09 we began noticing an uptick in short-context hallucinations on the nightly sampler for the 1k-sample set used by hosted-api smoke tests.
- Symptoms: model invents steps/details for queries that previously returned safe "I don't know" or short factual responses. Effect concentrated on prompts with < 80 token history.

Representative samples (prompt -> baseline -> current):
1) Prompt: "How do I reset my API key in the console?"
   Baseline: "Go to Console > Settings > API keys, choose rotate, follow confirmation."
   Current: "Open Console, go to Integrations, find your token under Apps, click Revoke then Regenerate — make sure to disable old tokens in IAM."
   Note: Current adds 'Integrations' and 'IAM' which our console doesn't have. Hallucination of UI paths.

2) Prompt: "Is redwood inference GDPR compliant for EU customers?"
   Baseline: "We offer VPC & private deployments and a Data Processing Addendum; talk to sales for a legal review."
   Current: "Yes — we are PIPEDA certified and maintain EU-only clusters in eu-west-1 with SOC3 audits."
   Note: Introduces incorrect compliance certs and region names.

Quick ad-hoc rubric (for short-context output quality) — 0..3 scores, used for rapid triage:
- 0 (OK): factual and concise, no invented entities/paths, aligns with our docs.
- 1 (minor): small wording issues or missing nuance but not introducing false artifacts.
- 2 (moderate): introduces at least one incorrect entity (service, cert, UI path) that could mislead a customer.
- 3 (bad): confidently asserts fabrication about product capabilities or compliance (likely regression).

Sampling notes and initial tally (nightly set, 100 short-context prompts):
- Feb 08 (pre-change): 4 responses with score >=2
- Feb 10: 18 responses with score >=2 (spike)
- Feb 20: 21 responses with score >=2 (persisting)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache invalidation change altered prefix retrieval for short histories causing model to lean on prior generation tokens as context — hallucination risk.
2) Batching scheduler change changed effective temperature/beam behaviour in the runtime optimization path for small N, exposing nondeterminism.
3) A model rollout (minor) coincided with runtime change — interaction effect.

Quick tests to run (small, fast):
- Re-run the nightly 1k sampler with kv-cache set to previous behaviour (env toggle) and current runtime scheduler to isolate which change correlates. (A/B: kv-old/scheduler-new vs kv-new/scheduler-new)
- Run deterministic seeding on a stable subset of 200 short prompts and compare token-level deltas.
- Capture KV entries (prefix hashes) for pairs where score >=2 to inspect whether wrong prefix was returned.

Instrumentation gaps I noticed:
- No easy flag to dump per-request KV cache hit keys in nightly harness; need a small patch to harness to log key fingerprints for failing samples.
- Sampler reports aggregated score counts but not the exact examples in the dashboard (we have them in the pipeline artifacts but not linked).

Immediate triage plan (this week):
- 1) Add temporary logging (kv key fingerprints + request id) to nightly sampler runner (small PR).
- 2) Re-run A/B described above, produce csv with prompt,id,baseline,current,score.
- 3) If A/B implicates KV change, revert cache invalidation to previous behaviour on a canary and monitor. If not, isolate scheduler by toggling batching flags.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- If these hallucinations only appear for short prompts, might be because the runtime falls back to cached partial generations (bad). 
- Check PR 1423 comments for any mention of hash collisions or key namespace changes; ping PR author if unclear.
- Could be related to quantization profile mismatch? less likely for short-context but keep in mind.

TODO (owner = me):
- [ ] Write tiny sampler patch to log kv fingerprints (due 2026-03-12)
- [ ] Kick off A/B with kv-old vs kv-new (target 1 hour run)
- [ ] Aggregate examples and score 200 samples manually using ad-hoc rubric
- [ ] Callout to #applied-ml on Slack with summary and attach csv

Slack / comms draft (for later):
"Heads up — seeing spike in short-context hallucinations after runtime push 1423. Running A/B to isolate kv-cache vs scheduler. Will share failing examples and quick triage steps by EOD. If you own PR 1423 please ping me. —Helena"

References / links to follow up:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/pr/1423
- JIRA: JIRA-8452 (nightly sampler regression)
- Nightly artifact path: s3://redwood-nightly/artifacts/short-context-sampler/2026-02-10/results.csv

End of scratchpad. Will refine rubric and move examples to a proper doc if we find root cause.
summary: Personal scratchpad capturing short-context hallucination regression after kv-cache + batching runtime changes; includes examples, ad-hoc rubric (0-3), hypotheses, quick tests and TODOs.
